text: Large Language Models, or LLMs, are computer programs that understand and generate human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns learned from huge amounts of training data, such as books, websites and articles. Users can improve results through prompt engineering, which means writing clear and specific instructions. LLMs are good at tasks like answering questions, summarising texts and translating languages. However, they have limits. They can sometimes produce wrong information, and they do not truly understand meaning. They simply repeat patterns from their training data, so users should always check important facts.
